# Reusable Hancom HWPX authoring guidance

This guidance is based on the Daechi feedback revision, using installed python-hwpx 6.6.0 and native Hancom 13, 0, 0, 3457. It describes observed capabilities and bounded checks, not independent certification of every source interpretation. The original PDF, delivered base HWPX and previous r4 PDF remain intact.

## Native equation dimensions and bearings

Hancom uses the serialized equation box when opening an externally authored HWPX. The installed python-hwpx estimator states explicitly that opening does not remeasure that box. A text/script estimator is therefore not equivalent to a native measured glyph/control extent.

For this document, `measure-native.ps1` created 201 distinct `(script, baseUnit)` combinations with native `EquationCreate`, then saved HWPX and PDF. `native-equation-metrics.actual.json` retains native `sz.width`, `sz.height`, `baseLine`, and the native left/right margins of 56 HWPUNIT. The cache also pins the Hancom version, equation font file SHA256 and measurement package SHA256. These are actual native layout measurements, not width guesses. Focused final-PDF inspection covers an overbar expression, a compound central-angle ratio followed by Korean text, and degree/unit expressions.

The first 10-point equality `bar {rm {AB}}=bar {rm {AC}}` changed from a base control width of 5021 HWPUNIT to a native measured width of 4245; this is a control-dimension observation, not a quality score or efficiency result. `author.py:measured_equation` now uses exact cached width/height/baseline/margins and fails on a missing script/size pair. No blanket 1.25 factor or trailing text-space safeguard remains.

For reuse:

1. Normalize only admitted syntax, preserving quoted text. Keep `rm`, `bar`, `ANGLE`, `BOT`, `==`, units and degree exponents structurally separate. Native `^{circ}` is used for degrees here.
2. Key every metric by exact script, baseUnit, equation font bytes, Hancom version and relevant equation style. Existing code stores script/baseUnit dictionary keys inside an environment-pinned cache; the caller must check the environment fingerprint before reuse. It is not a universal cross-version cache.
3. Batch only missing keys in one fresh owned native COM instance. Native Codex remains the tool owner. This is finite document automation, not another agent runtime.
4. Preserve native dimensions and baseline before changing margins. Inspect real glyph/control bearings when a particular symbol overhangs. Change only the measured offending case; do not shrink all objects or add arbitrary padding to every formula.
5. Recheck native wrapping for paragraphs that use new metrics. Reuse transcription and unrelated geometry evidence. A shared font or renderer change invalidates affected layout checks.

## Alignment inside editable frames

Hancom's official command documentation describes `EQALIGN` alignment around `&`, `MATRIX` with `&` for columns and `#` for rows, and `LCOL`/`RCOL` for column alignment. `LPILE`, `PILE`, and `RPILE` provide vertical stacking. The script editor uses `#` for line breaks. Korean text can be entered in the script editor; quoted strings in the observed samples remain text rather than mathematical identifiers.

Authoritative references, consulted for this revision:

- [Hancom equation commands](https://help.hancom.com/hoffice130_assistant/ko-KR/Hwp/insert/equation/equation%28explanation%29.htm)
- [Hancom script-entry rules](https://help.hancom.com/hoffice120/ko-KR/Hwp/insert/equation/equation%28rule%29.htm)
- [Hancom equation file specification, revision 1.3](https://cdn.hancom.com/link/docs/%ED%95%9C%EA%B8%80%EB%AC%B8%EC%84%9C%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC%ED%98%95%EC%8B%9D_%EC%88%98%EC%8B%9D_revision1.3.pdf).

The native samples are retained in `alignment.json`, `alignment-native-probe.png`, and `C:/Users/packr/Downloads/Daechi-feedback-20261022/native-equation-metrics-r1.{hwpx,pdf}`. Reuse the observed samples instead of researching syntax on each paper.

Q17 is one editable native equation inside a native frame:

```text
matrix {
  lcol { "(ㄱ) 사다리꼴" # "(ㄷ) 평행사변형" # "(ㅁ) 마름모" }
  lcol { "(ㄴ) 등변사다리꼴" # "(ㄹ) 직사각형" # "(ㅂ) 정사각형" }
}
```

The two columns and three rows are structural. They are not a sequence of proportional-font padding spaces. The observed native equation is 13556 by 3036 HWPUNIT at baseUnit 920. Native Korean equation typography can differ from body typography; do not substitute a screenshot to hide that difference.

The retained native `EQALIGN` sample is:

```text
eqalign {
  bar {rm {AB}} &= bar {rm {DC}} #
  bar {rm {AD}} &= bar {rm {BC}}
}
```

Q18 uses editable body text and native equations in ordered proof paragraphs with a common left origin. Its five answer blanks are actual inline rectangular native tables. This mixed-content implementation keeps the original sequence, Korean prose, diagram and blank frames editable. It does not force all prose into one equation. The diagram is inside the proof frame, and the proof frame is inside the full-question table. A future proof adapter can introduce relation-column alignment through `EQALIGN` where the source actually calls for stacked equation alignment; that change is not required for the current frame to be selectable and organized.

## One native table per complete question

The page template is a two-column native table. Each column contains two separate unfilled, borderless, inline 1x1 native question tables. Each question table owns its full stem, picture, native equations, all five choices and any source frames. All four outer question borders are `NONE`, with no `fillBrush`. White raster diagram backgrounds remain image pixels; transparent question-table shading does not make an embedded white PNG transparent.

The page's center rule belongs to the page template. The visible 보기/proof borders belong to their source frames. The question containers remain borderless. Native `pageBreak=NONE` and inline anchoring preserve a question's content as a unit; minimum height is a layout lower bound and may expand when content grows.

To copy a whole question, select its outer question table, rather than an inner blank or the page template. In a nested-table UI, the stem paragraph is the best starting context. The exact manual menu/key behavior can vary with Hancom settings. The native automation used and verified here is:

```text
SetPosBySet(questionCtrl.GetAnchorPos(0))
FindCtrl()                           // returns tbl for the selected question
block = GetTextFile("HWPML2X", "saveblock")
Clear(1)                             // owned scratch only
SetTextFile(block, "HWPML2X", "insertfile")
SaveAs(scratch, "HWPX", "")
```

Q18 was selected independently and transferred with its 17 equations, one picture and seven tables (question + proof frame + five blanks). A subsequent scratch edit added body text and a new native equation. The final artifact was not edited by this check. OS clipboard Copy/Paste was not invoked; selected-block native transfer is the behavior actually verified.

Hancom documents `HWPML2X` for format-preserving transfer; `GetTextFile`/`SetTextFile` do not support `HWPX` strings. The HWPX selected-block alternative is `FileSaveBlock_S` followed by `InsertFile`. Native automation references:

- [Hancom SetTextFile](https://developer.hancom.com/en-us/webhwp/devguide/hwpctrl/methods/settextfile)
- [Native selected-block HWPML2X discussion](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/hwpml2x/2973)
- [Native HWPX selected-block support and file-based alternative](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/gettextfile-hwpx-saveblock/3102)
- [Selecting a table from its anchor](https://forum.developer.hancom.com/t/topic/1086/2)

## Separate content, question layout and page template

- `content.ts` / `content.json`: source wording, math, choice order, point values and explicit underline spans.
- `figures.ts` / `figures/q*.svg`: constructed incidences, feet, centers, line styles, angle targets, fills and label presentation coordinates.
- `question-layout.json`: figure widths, local stem sizes, source-frame ownership and alignment policy.
- `page-template.json`: A4, columns, four-question grouping, logical order and first-slot minimum heights by column.
- `author.py`: finite native HWPX serialization; `question-bindings.actual.json` and `equation-bindings.actual.json` bind semantic scope to emitted control IDs.

Equal question count does not imply equal question height. Q17 is short; Q18 contains a proof. The current template uses two questions per column, with content-dependent minimum first-slot heights. Do not force Q18 into a rigid half-page box. Keep logical order 1,2,3,4 while original physical pages are read 1,2,4,3,5,6.

These values reproduce the current paper. They are not a general page optimizer. If text changes, measure the changed question, following slots in its column and the affected page. Keep semantic transcription and unchanged scenes. Global template changes require an all-page native contact-sheet check.

## Source typography and marks

Native underline runs preserve the confirmed negative emphasis in Q1, Q4, Q8, Q13, Q14 and Q18. Irregular extra emphasis near Q16/Q17 is retained as source-role uncertainty in `source-observations.actual.json`; it was not silently certified as printed. The source itself remains unchanged.

A dimension curve is not a geometric edge. An angle leader is not a parallel arrow. An angle sector fill is not a student's shaded solution region. Source role (`printed`, `student`, `uncertain`) is a different type axis from primitive kind (`line`, `arc`, `leader`, `fill`, `tick`, `label`). A geometry solver cannot establish which axis is printed.

## SVG rasterization and package checks

The initial MuPDF SVG trial converted dashed lines to solid strokes. The final adapter `render_figures.py` uses already installed librsvg/Cairo and preserves dash arrays, fills and leaders. No package was installed. Pin renderer identity and font resolution; an SVG source check alone cannot establish the embedded raster's line style.

The diagrams are raster pictures inside HWPX. Their source SVG and deterministic TypeScript remain editable outside Hancom; they are not native editable Hancom line objects. Body text, equations, table frames and blanks remain native editable objects.

Use one proportionate final pass: source/base hashes unchanged; XML/ZIP integrity; all 24 question containers and 120 choices; native metric readback; 21 pictures; six-page native coverage; one focused nested-question transfer. Repeat only for changed evidence or a discovered defect. `verification.actual.json` records the exact final hash and limits. No independent semantic AcceptanceDecision was synthesized.
